picks.line_source: DraftKings via VegasInsider (Sept 27, 9:24 p.m. ET); FanDuel -5.5; Circa opened -6.5
picks.case: Mississippi State is 4-0 straight up and 4-0 ATS and just erased a 24-17 fourth-quarter deficit to beat then-No. 25 Missouri 31-24, while Alabama's first true road pressure point comes against an unbeaten ranked opponent. The market agrees this is not a conventional two-score Alabama spot: Circa opened -6.5 and the number has been bet down to -6/-5.5.
picks.race_effect: The winner exits in control of the SEC West conversation; Alabama losing would hand its first conference loss to a division rival in Week 5.

picks.line_source: DraftKings and FanDuel via VegasInsider (Sept 27, 9:24 p.m. ET); Circa reference opener -3.5
picks.case: The classic sell-the-emotional-peak spot, with facts behind it: Florida is coming off a 52-28 emotional peak over No. 9 Ole Miss (35 second-half points), while Missouri led Mississippi State 24-17 into the fourth quarter before losing 31-24 — a closer team than its 3-1 record suggests. Missouri QB Austin Simmons produced nearly 300 yards and three touchdowns in that defeat (CBS).
picks.race_effect: A Missouri win re-tangles the SEC East and snaps Florida's playoff momentum a week after its signature win.

picks.line_source: DraftKings and FanDuel via VegasInsider (Sept 27, 9:24 p.m. ET); Circa opened -14.5 and was bet to -13 within 10 minutes — the board's clearest early sharp-resistance signal
picks.case: Iowa is 4-0, 3-1 ATS, and just won 20-19 at Michigan on a walk-off touchdown catch. The total sits at 45.5 — the slate's lowest among marquee games — and fewer projected possessions make Kinnick variance (turnovers, special teams, field position) disproportionately valuable. CBS notes Iowa has not lost by 14-plus since 2024 and not at home since 2021.
picks.race_effect: The loser of this top-14 game is effectively out of margin for error before mid-October; an Iowa win blows the Big Ten race open.

picks.line_source: DraftKings via VegasInsider (Sept 27, 9:24 p.m. ET); FanDuel -16.5; total fell from 50.5 opener to 49/49.5
picks.case: The price treats an improving 3-1 home team that has won three straight since Week 1 as essentially noncompetitive. Miami's 4-0 start is real (33.7-point average FBS margin) but the 52-3 statement came against Central Michigan, not a peer — and the falling total makes laying 17-plus harder, not easier.
picks.race_effect: A Clemson win would re-race the ACC and knock Miami from the unbeaten ranks; Miami winning in Death Valley would all but close the ACC regular-season conversation.

picks.line_source: FOX board Sept 28; DraftKings Sept 27 snapshot was Kentucky +3.5 — the hook has been shaved
picks.case: The honest case is the number: a road underdog of one field goal against an opponent ESPN's FPI ranks only 21st nationally (Kentucky 47th) — closer than public perception of an unranked road team. The market moving from +3.5 to +3 reads more like a genuine toss-up than an obvious home win.
picks.race_effect: Both teams enter with conference losses already; the winner stays on the SEC East undercard, the loser falls two back.

trap.why: The public-facing upset story — Death Valley, Clemson's three straight wins, Miami hasn't won there since 2010 — is irresistible, but the evidence backs the favorite: Miami is 4-0 beating FBS opponents by 33.7 points per game, while Clemson's recovery has not erased its 52-10 Week 1 loss to LSU. Circa opened Miami -16, briefly went to -17.5, settled -16.5, and DraftKings later showed -17.5 — the market accepting Miami's class, not buying a Clemson renaissance. Lay the points rather than chase the atmosphere.
